name: continuous-pagination
title: Continuous Pagination
description: A row of five numbered page tiles between left and right chevrons; the current page wears a dark glossy raised tile that springs to whichever number you click.
use: A list or gallery is split into a handful of pages and you want a tactile page switcher.
avoid: Hundreds of pages: it renders every number, so the row grows unbounded and overflows.
a11y: Number buttons read as text, but the chevrons have no labels and the active page is not exposed as current. (keyboard: yes, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Nine rounded square buttons in a row on black: a chevron-left, five numbered tiles and a chevron-right. The active number sits on a darker, slightly proud tile with a highlighted top edge, soft drop shadow and a faint sheen, while the other tiles stay flat grey with muted digits.
behaves: Clicking a number or an arrow springs the raised tile to the new page, lifting and settling into place. Inactive tiles rise on hover and every button compresses on press, while a slow diagonal shine crosses the active tile every few seconds.
customise: Total page count and the starting page are props; the tile size, glossy gradient, spacing and shine timing are fixed in the source.
weight: light: Five small tiles and one looping shine with no canvas or data work.
demo: Pages 1 to 5 with the second page active.
issues: The slow shine on the active tile keeps running even when the page is idle.
polishWhy: Tight, tactile pager with a convincing glossy tile; the endless sheen is slightly distracting.
